chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Husayn from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a female slave who belongs to a woman, so she sells her, he said: 'There is no objection to him having intercourse with her without requiring her to complete her waiting period (istibra').

key_terms.يَسْتَبْرِئَهَا: he requires her to complete istibra (waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on having intercourse with a female slave without waiting for istibra?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when a free woman sells her female concubine, the new owner may consummate the marriage without observing the *istibra* (waiting period), as the transfer of ownership from a free woman to another owner does not require the same waiting period as a slave being sold to a new master. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of *ummahat al-awlad* (mothers of children) and concubines in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that *istibra* is primarily required to establish paternity when the master changes, but is waived here due to the specific context of the sale between owners. The hadith underscores the practical implications for lineage verification (*lhuq al-awlad*) and the flexibility of marital laws regarding concubinage in early Islamic society.
